new_findings.summary: The guarantee 'an outage is blamed on the caller' is UNGUARDED — the harness scores it MISS.
new_findings.detail: Mutating away the psycopg.OperationalError branch in refusals.classify does not fail test_refusals.py::test_the_database_being_unreachable_is_not_the_callers_fault. With the branch removed, an OperationalError falls through to the generic psycopg.Error catch-all and still returns 500 'broke', so the test's status and kind assertions hold. What the mutation actually destroys is the SEPARATE reason sentence and the stderr log line, neither of which the test asserts — correctly, since the house rule forbids testing wording.
new_findings.pre_existing: PROVEN, not assumed. Re-ran the mutation against refusals.py at HEAD, with this pass's changes stashed: it also returned 500 'broke'. This is not a regression introduced here.
new_findings.why_it_was_invisible: The harness had been aborting in preflight, so all 36 doorway rows were unevaluated. Repairing the gate (WP-001) is what made this visible — which is the argument for sequencing WP-001 first, now demonstrated rather than asserted.
new_findings.not_fixed_here: Out of scope for every package in this plan. Closing it means finding an observable difference between the two paths that is not message text, or accepting the row as unguardable and retiring it with a reason. That is an owner decision of the same shape as D4.
